<!--
Measured, not read: a figure drawn by a code chunk keeps its apa-note inside
the float, as a figure written in markdown does.

The note was written after \end{figure}. In a manuscript the figure is set
[H], in place, but a page could still break between it and a note outside
it: the figure after 18 lines below ended its page and its note began the
next. A figure that floats, in a journal or with floatsintext: false, left
the note behind in the text altogether.

The first page sets the same picture twice, from a chunk and from markdown,
so its note must sit the same distance under the caption in both (knitr
sets the picture 4.48in wide, and the markdown one is given that width). The
markdown figure follows the chunk directly: a filter in Data-Wise/apa-layout
that moved \end{figure} past whatever note came next took the markdown
figure, note and all, for the chunk's note and nested one float in the other.
-->

```{r}
#| label: fig-chunkone
#| fig-cap: "Chunkcap caption"
#| apa-note: "Chunknote words."
knitr::include_graphics("sampleimage.png")
```
